title: Atlas: hybrid on-premises and Azure warehouse system, noisy dialogue
proves: Fillers, rhetorical questions, Windows/MSI releases, a DR plan that was never tested.
transcript:
Right, so, um, Atlas is the warehouse management system for the two distribution centres in Leeds and Bristol. Pickers use handheld scanners that talk to it all day.

It's hybrid, you know. The core app runs on four Windows servers in our own data centre with SQL Server 2019 underneath. Orders come in from the web shop through Azure Service Bus, and a small integration service on an Azure VM pulls them off the queue and pushes them into Atlas.

So how do we release? Azure DevOps builds the MSI and a release pipeline installs it on the servers one at a time behind the load balancer. If a release goes bad, we reinstall the previous MSI, it's kept in the drop folder.

What do we monitor with? Zabbix for the servers, and there's a Service Bus dead letter alert in Azure Monitor. If the dead letter count goes above zero someone needs to look the same day.

The classic failure is scanners losing their session after the Wi-Fi drops and pickers getting logged out. Restarting the scanner app fixes it, you don't need to touch the server. The other one is order messages going to the dead letter queue because of a bad SKU, and you resubmit them from Service Bus Explorer once the SKU is fixed.

Backups: SQL Server full backup every night and log backups every fifteen minutes, copied to Azure Blob storage. Do we have a DR site? No, um, not really, the plan is to rebuild the servers from the VM templates, and that's never been tested.

Please don't reindex the big tables during shift hours, the scanners time out. And never restart the integration VM during the evening dispatch window.

Peak is November and December, and the evening dispatch between six and nine is the busiest hour every day.

Security, uh, everything sits behind the corporate firewall, and the integration VM uses a managed identity for Service Bus.

Is there a test environment? Yes, one UAT server with last month's data.

The warehouse systems team owns Atlas. Out of hours call the service desk, they page whoever is on call, and the escalation manager is Tom Briggs.

Budget-wise, we were asked to reserve the Azure VM for three years, but that hasn't been approved yet.

Open items, the scanner firmware upgrade is planned for next quarter and it's not assigned to anyone.

For the first couple of weeks shadow the morning shift support, and you need a domain admin account and VPN.
